name: Tax Exemption for WooCommerce
author: Elliot Sowersby / RelyWP

sections.description:
Let your customers declare that they are exempt from tax on WooCommerce checkout, provide the details to back it up, and have tax removed from their order automatically.

This is useful if you have some customers that are eligible to be exempt from tax on your products, for example for the purpose of disability VAT exemption or charity VAT relief, or business customers supplying a VAT number.

Getting Started

Simply install the “Tax Exemption plugin for WooCommerce” plugin, and visit the “Tax Exemption” settings page under “WooCommerce” in the WordPress admin.

Configure the plugin settings as required:

  • Enable or disable the tax exemption feature.
  • Select the tax class to use for the Tax / VAT exemption.
  • Select the location on checkout to display the tax exemption fields.
  • Show the tax exemption checkbox and fields on the cart page too, and choose where.
  • Enable or disable removal of tax on shipping for exempt customers.
  • Enable or disable the tax exemption fields on the “My Account” page.
  • Choose which details to collect – the name and reason fields can each be shown, hidden, or made required.
  • Collect a registration number (VAT number, charity number, ABN and more) and choose which types you accept.
  • Get an email whenever a tax exempt order is placed.
  • Customise the text/labels used throughout the plugin.

Your customers will then be able to select the “I want to claim tax exemption” checkbox on the checkout page, and enter their tax exemption details.

Tax will be removed from their order if this is checked and they have entered their details successfully.

Where The Form Appears

The tax exemption form works on the classic checkout, the WooCommerce block checkout, the cart page, and the “My Account” page, for both guests and logged in customers.

You can also place it anywhere else on your site with the [tefw_exemption_form] shortcode.

Managing Exempt Customers & Orders

  • Exempt Customers – a searchable list of every customer claiming tax exemption, along with their details. Customers can be added and edited here directly.
  • Exempt Orders – every order placed with tax exemption, filterable by date.
  • If an order is marked as tax / VAT exempt, this will be shown on the admin order details page, where you can see the tax exempt details. An optional column on the orders list marks which orders were exempt.
  • Each customer’s exemption details can also be viewed and edited from their WordPress user profile.
  • Tax exemption details are included in WordPress personal data exports and erasure requests.

PRO Version

The PRO version offers several additional features including:

  • Registration number verification (VAT, charity, ABN, GSTIN and more).
  • Live lookups against the official registers – VIES, HMRC, the Australian Business Register and the Charity Commission.
  • Automatic approval for customers whose number verifies.
  • Consultation references recorded as proof that a number was checked.
  • Re-check a customer’s stored number at any time.
  • Option to show ex-tax prices to exempt customers across the whole store.
  • Optional “inc/ex tax” price toggle for every visitor.
  • Custom tax exemption form fields.
  • Tax exemption certificate upload field.
  • Tax exemption expiration date field.
  • Automatic expiry reminder & expired notification emails.
  • Customisable exemption request, approval and decline emails.
  • Default validity period (auto-calculate expiration dates).
  • Tax exemption city/state field.
  • Tax exemption fields on registration form.
  • Exemption status management for admins.
  • Only allow exemption for approved users.
  • Hide the tax exemption fields on checkout.
  • Only remove tax from specific products.
  • Only allow exemption for logged in users.
  • Only allow exemption for selected user roles.
  • Only allow exemption for selected countries.
  • Only allow exemption for selected states/cities.
  • Customize the tax class for each user.
  • Export CSV files of exempt customers.
  • Export CSV files of exempt orders.
  • Integration with “AvaTax”.

UPGRADE TO PRO
sections.faq:
What is the purpose of this plugin?

Tax Exemption for WooCommerce allows customers to declare their tax exemption status on the WooCommerce checkout page, and provide their tax exemption details. This is useful for customers that are eligible for tax relief, such as charities or disabled individuals.

How does the tax exemption work?

When a customer selects the “I want to claim tax exemption” checkbox on the checkout page, they will be able to enter their tax exemption details. If they have entered their details successfully, tax will be removed from their order.

Is it compatible with Stripe Tax?

Yes, the plugin is compatible with Stripe Tax. If you are using the Stripe Tax plugin, it will automatically remove tax from orders for customers that have declared their tax exemption status.

Is it compatible with AvaTax?

The PRO version of the plugin is compatible with AvaTax. If you are using the AvaTax integration, it will automatically remove tax from orders for customers that have declared their tax exemption status.

Is it compatible with WooCommerce Subscriptions?

Yes, the plugin is compatible with WooCommerce Subscriptions.

Is it compatible with WooCommerce Block Checkout?

Yes, the plugin is fully compatible with WooCommerce Block Checkout.

Customers can enable and disable tax exemption directly on the block checkout page, and tax will be removed from their order if they are exempt.

Is it compatible with other checkout plugins?

The plugin is designed to be compatible with the default WooCommerce checkout and WooCommerce Block Checkout.

It will also work fine with many other popular checkout plugins like CheckoutWC and Flux Checkout.

If you are using a different checkout plugin and having issues, please get in touch.

Do you provide support?

Yes. If you need any help setting up the plugin, please free to get in touch and we’ll be happy to help!

How can I report feature issues/bugs with the plugin?

You can report feature bugs by creating a support ticket. Please provide as much information as possible to make it easier for us to find a solution for you.

Does this plugin use a 3rd party service?

Freemius: The plugin uses the Freemius SDK for optional usage tracking and licensing of PRO features; see Freemius privacy and terms for details.

Font Awesome: The plugin uses Font Awesome (free) for icons; see Font Awesome privacy and terms for details.

Official registers (PRO): if you enable registration number verification and switch on one of the official registers, the registration number the customer entered is sent to that register to be checked. Every register is off by default, and none is ever contacted unless you turn it on and supply its credentials:

  • EU VAT numbers are sent to the European Commission’s VIES service; see the VIES service and the European Commission privacy policy.
  • UK VAT numbers are sent to HMRC’s “Check a UK VAT number” API; see the HMRC API documentation and the GOV.UK privacy notice.
  • Australian ABNs are sent to the Australian Business Register; see the ABR and its privacy policy.
  • England & Wales charity numbers are sent to the Charity Commission Register API; see the Charity Commission API portal and its personal information charter.

Only the registration number itself is sent, together with the credentials you configured for that register – optionally including your own VAT number, which is what makes VIES and HMRC return a consultation reference as proof of the check. No other customer or order data leaves your site.

How does registration number verification work?

Every number is first checked against its own format, and against its official check digit where the number type has one – UK VAT, Australian ABNs, India GSTIN, New Zealand IRD and Canadian Business Numbers all do. That needs no setup or account, and catches effectively every typo and invented number.

On top of that, PRO can look the number up against its official register in real time, for the four registers listed above. You choose whether a number that is actively rejected simply gets flagged for your review, or blocks the customer from claiming exemption.

A register being temporarily unreachable is never treated as an invalid number. Customers are only ever blocked when a register actively rejects their number and you have chosen to block on failure.

How can I report security bugs?

You can report security bugs through the Patchstack Vulnerability Disclosure Program. The Patchstack team helps validate, triage and handle any security vulnerabilities. Report a security vulnerability.
sections.changelog:
Version 3.4.0 – 6th November 2026

  • New: (PRO) Added a “Tax Exempt Product” option to each variation of a variable product, when “Specific products only” is on. Choose “Yes” or “No” to decide for that variation, or leave it on “Same as parent product” (the default, so existing variations are unchanged) to follow the “Tax Exempt Product” box on the product’s “General” tab.
  • New: (PRO) Added an “Eligible Products Only” option to the “Price Toggle” settings, shown when “Specific products only” is on and ticked by default. The price toggle then only switches prices on products marked as “Tax Exempt Product”: other products keep their normal price, and the toggle is not shown on their product pages or on a shop listing with none of them. Untick it to switch every product’s price as before.
  • New: Added the “tefw_product_is_exempt_eligible” filter, to decide which products are eligible for exemption with “Specific products only” on (for example by category), and the “tefw_price_display_applies_to_product” filter, to decide which products’ prices may be shown excluding tax.
  • Tweak: Every check of whether a product is eligible for exemption (the tax on each item, shipping, the “eligible product required” checks, admin order recalculation and price display) now uses the same rule.
  • Fix: (PRO) Fixed an issue where “Show Ex-Tax Prices To Exempt Customers” showed every product excluding tax with “Specific products only” on, including products the customer would still be charged tax on. Those products are now shown at their normal price with your store’s own price suffix, and the “Prices are shown excluding tax” notice is not shown where no price is. A variable product’s price range is only shown excluding tax when all of its variations are eligible; each variation’s own price follows that variation.

Version 3.3.0 – 25th October 2026

  • New: (PRO) Added a “Who Can Claim Exemption” option to the “General” tab. Choose “Admins only” if customers should not be able to claim tax exemption themselves: only the customers you mark exempt on the “Exempt Customers” page are exempted, automatically at checkout, and the exemption checkbox and fields on the cart, checkout, My Account page and registration form are turned off. Their exemption is applied even if details such as a certificate, exemption number or expiry date have not been filled in, while an expiry date that has passed still ends it. Your settings for those are kept, for if you switch back to “Customers”.
  • New: Added a “Tax exempt order” Yes/No option to the “Tax Exemption” box when creating or editing an order in the admin, to exempt (or stop exempting) that one order, including guest orders, without changing the customer’s own exemption. The taxes are recalculated as soon as it is changed. It follows the selected customer’s exemption until you change it. The “Edit Order Page” setting now only decides whether the exemption details are shown in the box.
  • New: Added the “tefw_express_checkout_selectors” filter, to set which express payment button containers are paused while the classic checkout updates its totals.
  • Tweak: Redesigned the “Exempt Customers” and “Exempt Orders” pages, with a cleaner layout and new tools: status tabs with counts (and the number of customers awaiting approval on the menu), Approve / Decline links on pending customers, bulk actions, sortable columns, search by exemption name, reason or registration number, an order status filter and date range presets, “Status” and “Total” columns on orders, Screen Options to choose the columns and rows per page, a customer search in the “Add Customer” form, a “Date Added” that shows when the customer was added, and CSV exports that match the filters on screen. Also fixes editing a customer clearing their expiration date, guest customers being shown another guest’s certificate and custom fields, and the missing search box on “Exempt Orders”.
  • Tweak: Looking up a customer’s tax exemption when they are selected on the admin Edit Order page now requires permission to edit orders.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where the “Tax Exemption” box was not shown on the admin Edit Order page when WooCommerce’s High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS) is enabled.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where saving or recalculating an order in the admin changed its tax exemption to match the customer’s account as it is now, rather than what the order was placed with – so an exempt order for a customer who was no longer exempt was marked as not exempt while its tax stayed removed, and the reverse. Orders now keep their exemption unless it is changed with “Tax exempt order”, and the “Tax Exemption” box notes when the customer’s own exemption has changed since.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where orders created in the admin were tax exempt for customers whose exemption had expired, been declined, or was still awaiting approval.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where changing an order’s customer in the admin to a tax exempt customer, from a guest or a customer who was not exempt, took a second save to exempt the order. Changing an exempt order’s customer to a guest now also removes the exemption.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue on the classic checkout where typing into the “Name” or “Reason” field and then clicking “Place Order” straight away did nothing – no order was placed and no error was shown. The fields are now saved shortly after typing stops, rather than as soon as they lose focus.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue on the classic checkout where clicking an express payment button (Apple Pay, Google Pay, Link) while the order totals were updating, such as straight after ticking or unticking the tax exemption box, left the page covered and unclickable, or could charge the total from before the update. The buttons are now paused until the totals have updated, including the first update when the page loads, and an update that fails is tried once more.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where express payment buttons on the classic checkout used an outdated “Name” and “Reason”, so an order could go through with a required field the customer had just cleared, or be saved with the previous values.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where ticking or unticking the tax exemption box on the classic checkout could sometimes be undone by a second request made at the same time. This request is now only made when Flux Checkout is active.
  • Fix: Fixed a possible “Cannot redeclare” fatal error with the Stripe Tax integration when tax was calculated more than once in the same request.

Version 3.2.0 – 7th October 2026

  • New: (PRO) Added “Allowed File Types” on the “Certificates” tab, so customers can upload their certificate as a JPG, PNG or Word document as well as a PDF. Each file is checked to be the type it claims to be. Developers can use the “tefw_certificate_allowed_mimes” filter; HTML, SVG and script files are never accepted.
  • New: Added a “Remove Tax on Fees” option to the “General” tab, to also remove tax from fees added to the cart by other plugins (such as handling or payment fees) for tax exempt customers.
  • New: Added a “Save Details to Account” option to the “Display Locations” tab. Choose “Customers only” if your staff place orders for customers while logged in as themselves, so each customer’s exemption details are saved to their order rather than to the staff account and filled in on the next order.
  • New: (PRO) Added a “Hide Selected Locations Note” option under “Custom Text” > “Restriction Notes”, to hide the “Tax exemption will only apply in: …” note while keeping the country and state restrictions.
  • New: (PRO) Added a “Reply-To Address” setting for the tax exemption emails. Replies to the admin request email now go to the customer who made the request.
  • New: Added the tefw_render_order_exemption_details( $order, $plain_text ) function, to show an order’s tax exemption details in your own email templates, such as an overridden admin-new-order.php.
  • Tweak: The “Add New / Update Customer” form on the “Exempt Customers” page now accepts an email address as well as a username, and explains when no account is found.
  • Tweak: Customers outside the allowed user roles can no longer submit a tax exemption request from the cart or My Account.
  • Tweak: The plugin’s own icon is now shown on the Account page.
  • Tweak: Updated the translation template, and made the remaining messages shown by the plugin’s scripts translatable.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where the required “Name” and “Reason” fields were not enforced on the classic checkout, the block checkout, or express payment buttons (Apple Pay, Google Pay, Link), so a tax exempt order could be placed with them left empty.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue on the cart and block checkout where a customer whose saved exemption details were missing a required field was shown the tax exemption box unticked, but was still treated as tax exempt and could not place their order. The totals now always match the box.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where tax was removed from shipping, but not from the products, for customers who are not eligible for tax exemption, such as those still awaiting approval.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where checkout builders such as FunnelKit showed the required field marker as raw HTML, e.g. “Full Name *”. Required fields are now marked by WooCommerce in the same way as its own fields.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where placing an order on the block checkout could clear a tax exemption granted by the store, save “undefined” as the customer’s name and reason, and send the store an unwanted “Tax Exemption Request” email – particularly when the checkbox is hidden on checkout.
  • Fix: (PRO) Fixed an issue where, with “Require Manual Approval” enabled, customers awaiting approval and guests saw an empty box on the block checkout instead of the “Want to claim tax exemption? Click here” message.
  • Fix: (PRO) Fixed an issue where the block checkout ignored the custom URL set for the “Exemption Message”, always linking to the My Account page.
  • Fix: (PRO) Fixed an issue where customers awaiting approval were told “Tax exemption is enabled” on the block checkout.
  • Fix: (PRO) Fixed an issue where the “Hide this message from checkout if exemption is enabled” option had no effect on the block checkout.
  • Fix: (PRO) Fixed an issue where, with “Specific products only” enabled, visiting the cart page removed tax from every product in the order – and from shipping – rather than just the eligible products.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where the cart page removed tax from shipping even with “Remove Tax on Shipping” disabled.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where the admin “New Order” email and the order received page did not show the tax exemption details for some exempt orders, including “Specific products only” orders and stores that hide the “Name” field. Every detail the order has is now shown, and plain text emails get a plain text version.
  • Fix: (PRO) Fixed an issue where the “Tax Exemption Approved” and “Tax Exemption Declined” emails were only sent when using the buttons in the admin request email. They are now sent whenever a customer’s status changes, including from the “Exempt Customers” page, the user profile and registration number auto-approval.
  • Fix: (PRO) Fixed an issue where customers claiming tax exemption on the registration form were not set to “Pending”, and no request email was sent, when “Require Manual Approval” is enabled.
  • Fix: (PRO) Fixed an issue where a certificate uploaded on the registration form was not saved.
  • Fix: Fixed an “Undefined variable $show_exemption” PHP warning on the checkout page.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where HTML in the “My Account Description” setting was removed when saving. If you had used HTML there, please enter it again.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where the “Checkbox Description” was not shown under the checkbox on the classic checkout.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where an order could record tax exemption for a customer who was not eligible for it, so the order screens and emails disagreed with the tax charged.
  • Fix: (PRO) Fixed an issue where saving the block checkout’s tax exemption form cleared the customer’s AvaTax exemption type.
  • Security: (PRO) Fixed an issue where the “Tax Exemption Approved” and “Tax Exemption Declined” emails sent from the approve/decline buttons in the admin request email could include the plugin’s settings.

Version 3.1.1 – 17th September 2026

  • Fix: Fixed an issue where the “Exempt Customers” page could time out on stores with a large number of customers, showing “The customer list could not be loaded (HTTP 500)” instead of the customer list. The “Expiring Soon” and “Expired” filters and the CSV export were affected in the same way.
  • Fix: (PRO) Fixed an issue where uploading a certificate on the checkout page always failed with “Your certificate could not be uploaded. Please try again.”
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where express checkout buttons (Apple Pay, Google Pay and Link from the Stripe or WooPayments plugins) kept the tax exempt total after the tax exemption box was unticked on the checkout page, and could show a different total to the order review until the page was refreshed. Unticking the box now removes the exemption from the order straight away, including for customers who are exempt on their account and had visited the cart page first.
  • Fix: (PRO) Fixed an issue where customers who are tax exempt on their account were still charged tax on the block checkout when the “Hide Checkbox On Checkout” option was enabled, even though the cart page had already removed the tax. The exemption is now taken from the customer’s account in the same way as the classic checkout.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where a customer whose exemption was still pending approval, or had been declined, could be tax exempt on the block checkout. The block checkout now applies the same approval, user role and expiry rules as the cart and the classic checkout.

Version 3.1.0 – 10th September 2026

  • New: (PRO) Added a “Price Display” settings tab with an option to show prices excluding tax to customers who are already tax exempt – across the shop, product pages and widgets, not just at the cart and checkout – so the price they browse is the price they pay.
  • New: (PRO) Added an optional price toggle letting every visitor switch between prices including and excluding tax. Place it above the shop listing, on product pages, or anywhere with the [tefw_price_toggle] shortcode. Both prices are rendered into the page and swapped in the browser, so it works on cached pages with no price flashing before it settles. The toggle changes what is displayed only – tax is still removed by the tax exemption form as usual.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where activating the PRO plugin failed with a fatal error if the free version was still active.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where an exempt customer could still be charged tax on their order total, even though the exemption had been applied to the products.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where a customer’s tax exemption could be cleared part way through checkout by a third-party checkout or payment plugin.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where updating to 3.0.0 made the exemption certificate mandatory on stores that had never asked for one, quietly removing exemption from customers without a certificate on file.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where the customer’s tax exempt flag was cleared on every view of the checkout page, which could leave shipping tax charged to exempt customers.
  • Fix: (PRO) Fixed an issue where the daily expiry check permanently switched off a customer’s tax exemption, and nothing switched it back on when they renewed.
  • Fix: (PRO) Fixed an issue where a customer’s status stayed on “Expired” after their exemption had been renewed, so they were still charged tax.
  • Fix: (PRO) Fixed an issue where switching on the “Expiration Date” field stopped tax exemption working for existing customers who had no expiration date saved.
  • Fix: (PRO) Fixed an issue where an expired tax exemption was still applied on the block checkout.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where the “Exempt Customers” page could hang on “Loading…” and never show the customer list.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where the “Guest Customers” list on the “Exempt Customers” page was always empty.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where the “Last Exempt Order” column was empty, and its links broken, on stores using High-Performance Order Storage.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where a store with a large number of tax exempt guest orders could run out of memory building the “Guest Customers” list.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where the “Exempt Customers” page could time out on stores using the AvaTax integration.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where turning off the “Enable Tax Exemption” option left the “Exempt Customers” page unable to load, save or export anything.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where shop managers were shown links to plugin pages they were not allowed to open.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where changing a customer’s status reported “Failed to update status” when they were already on the status chosen.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where saving a customer from the “Add New / Update Customer” form gave no response at all when the save failed.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where the free version’s “Exempt Customers” table was missing two column headings.
  • Fix: (PRO) Fixed an issue where a customer could not delete their own tax exemption certificate from the My Account page, always seeing “Access denied”.
  • Fix: (PRO) Fixed an issue, introduced in 3.0.0, where uploading a tax exemption certificate at checkout failed with “Your certificate could not be uploaded”.
  • Fix: (PRO) The free version is now automatically deactivated if it is still active when PRO is activated, since only one is ever meant to run at a time.

Version 3.0.0 – 31st July 2026

  • New: Added an option to show a “Registration Number” field to the tax exemption form, so customers can supply a VAT number, charity number, ABN, GSTIN, EIN, resale certificate number and more. Choose which number types your store accepts on the new “Registration Number” settings tab; tick a single type and the type dropdown is hidden entirely so customers just see one field.
  • New: The registration number is shown alongside the other exemption details everywhere they already appear – the customer’s account, the Exempt Customers and Exempt Orders pages and their CSV exports, the admin order screen, and the admin notification emails.
  • New: (PRO) Added registration number verification. Every number is checked against its own format and checksum rules, and the types that have an official register can be looked up live: EU VAT via VIES, UK VAT via HMRC, Australian ABNs via the ABR, and English & Welsh charity numbers via the Charity Commission. Each number type is its own row on the settings tab, and the types with a register expand to hold that register’s setup, so everything for a given type lives in one place.
  • New: (PRO) Added an “Auto-approve on Success” option. When a customer’s number verifies, their exemption is approved automatically. Numbers that fail are left pending for you to review rather than being declined outright.
  • New: (PRO) Successful VIES and HMRC checks record a consultation reference against the customer and the order – the evidence you need to show you verified a customer’s VAT number.
  • New: (PRO) Added a “Re-check” button on the customer profile and the Exempt Customers page to re-verify a stored number on demand.
  • New: (PRO) The verification badge now explains itself on hover, wherever it is shown: which official register the number was looked up in – or that only its checksum or format could be checked, and why – along with the name the register holds for it, the consultation reference and when it was last checked.
  • New: (PRO) Added automatic certificate/exemption expiry reminder emails. When the “Expiration Date” field is enabled, you can now send customers reminder emails a configurable number of days before their tax exemption expires (e.g. 30, 7 and 1 days before), each with a link to renew their details on the My Account page.
  • New: (PRO) Added an optional “Tax Exemption Expired” email, sent once to the customer when their exemption lapses.
  • New: (PRO) Added an “Expiring Soon” / “Expired” filter and status badges to the “Exempt Customers” admin page, so you can quickly see which exemptions need attention.
  • New: (PRO) Added a “Send Reminder” button on the “Exempt Customers” admin page to manually send an expiry reminder email to a customer.
  • New: (PRO) Added an optional daily admin digest email summarising exemptions that are expiring soon or have expired.
  • New: (PRO) Added an optional “Default Validity Period” setting. When enabled, exemption expiration dates are calculated automatically (e.g. valid for 12 months from setup/renewal) and the manual expiration date field is hidden from customers.
  • New: Added two new customer emails (“Tax Exemption Expiring Soon” and “Tax Exemption Expired”) to the Emails settings tab, with new {expiration_date}, {days_until_expiry} and {renew_url} merge tags.
  • New: Tax exemption is now applied on accelerated/express checkout (Apple Pay, Google Pay, Stripe Link and similar), where the normal checkout fields never load and tax was previously charged in full. A logged in customer’s saved exemption is used, and is still checked against their approval status, allowed user roles and expiration date before any tax is removed.
  • Tweak: Redesigned the admin settings page.
  • Tweak: (PRO) A register being temporarily unreachable is never treated as an invalid number. Customers are only ever blocked when a register actively rejects their number and you have chosen to block on failure – VIES member state services go offline regularly, and a checkout should not fail with them.
  • Tweak: The tax exemption checkbox and form are now shown directly on the WooCommerce block checkout by default, and are no longer a beta feature. The “[Beta] Block Checkout: Checkbox + Form” setting has been removed as it is now always enabled.
  • Tweak: The “Settings on My Account Page” option can now be turned off while using the block checkout. It was previously forced on and locked, as the block checkout relied on linking customers to the My Account page.
  • Tweak: Standardised expiry date comparisons to use the site timezone (current_time) for consistency.
  • Tweak: (PRO) Expired exemptions are now deactivated by the daily expiry scan, rather than waiting until the customer next reaches the checkout page. This keeps the “Exempt Customers” list accurate and makes sure a lapsed exemption cannot be used on express checkout.
  • Tweak: (PRO) The “Tax Exemption Expired” email is only sent for exemptions that lapsed within the last 30 days, so turning the feature on cannot email years of previously expired customers in one go. Use the “tefw_expired_email_max_age_days” filter to change the window.
  • Tweak: (PRO) The admin expiry digest email now lists at most 100 customers per section and reports how many more were not shown, so stores with a large number of exempt customers still get a usable email. Use the “tefw_expiry_digest_max_rows” filter to change the limit.
  • Tweak: (PRO) The “Exempt Customers” list now also matches customers on their expiration date, so anyone whose exemption has lapsed stays visible under the “Expired” filter.
  • Tweak: (PRO) Where an exemption certificate is required but there is no upload field on the page being submitted (the cart checkbox, block checkout, or checkout with “Show on Checkout” disabled), the message now points the customer to the “Tax Exemption” page in “My Account” instead of only repeating that a certificate is needed.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where the Emails settings tab accordions would not open, and several other settings (Custom Text restriction notes, Stripe Tax, Block Checkout and AvaTax enforcement, and the selected states options) would not show or hide correctly, caused by a JavaScript error on the plugin settings page.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where the “Tax Exemption” tab could be missing from the My Account menu on block-based or page-builder account pages, even though the endpoint page loaded correctly, by registering the endpoint with WooCommerce’s query var system.
  • Fix: Fixed an issue where a product’s tax class could be permanently changed to the tax exemption class. The exemption is only ever applied while a customer is shopping, but the exempt tax class could previously be picked up in the WordPress admin and by external tools, so using Quick Edit or Bulk Edit on the Products list, importing products, or syncing products through the REST API could save it to the product for good. The exemption is now limited to the storefront, cart and checkout only.
  • Fix: Fixed the excessive spacing above and below the tax exemption message (“Want to claim tax exemption? Click here”) on checkout, caused by line break tags being added around the message.
  • Fix: (PRO) Fixed an issue where the “Required” setting for exemption certificates was not enforced on block checkout, so customers could tick the tax exemption checkbox and place an order without uploading a certificate. The certificate is now required on the cart and block checkout as well, and the order is blocked if one is missing.
  • Fix: (PRO) Fixed an issue where a failed certificate upload on checkout (for example a file that was not a PDF, or was over the maximum upload size) was treated as successful, allowing the order to be placed with no certificate actually saved. Failed uploads now show the reason and the certificate is re-requested.

short_description: Tax Exemption plugin for WooCommerce. Allow customers to declare tax / VAT exemption eligibility, and provide tax exemption details.
description:
Let your customers declare that they are exempt from tax on WooCommerce checkout, provide the details to back it up, and have tax removed from their order automatically.

This is useful if you have some customers that are eligible to be exempt from tax on your products, for example for the purpose of disability VAT exemption or charity VAT relief, or business customers supplying a VAT number.

Getting Started

Simply install the “Tax Exemption plugin for WooCommerce” plugin, and visit the “Tax Exemption” settings page under “WooCommerce” in the WordPress admin.

Configure the plugin settings as required:

  • Enable or disable the tax exemption feature.
  • Select the tax class to use for the Tax / VAT exemption.
  • Select the location on checkout to display the tax exemption fields.
  • Show the tax exemption checkbox and fields on the cart page too, and choose where.
  • Enable or disable removal of tax on shipping for exempt customers.
  • Enable or disable the tax exemption fields on the “My Account” page.
  • Choose which details to collect – the name and reason fields can each be shown, hidden, or made required.
  • Collect a registration number (VAT number, charity number, ABN and more) and choose which types you accept.
  • Get an email whenever a tax exempt order is placed.
  • Customise the text/labels used throughout the plugin.

Your customers will then be able to select the “I want to claim tax exemption” checkbox on the checkout page, and enter their tax exemption details.

Tax will be removed from their order if this is checked and they have entered their details successfully.

Where The Form Appears

The tax exemption form works on the classic checkout, the WooCommerce block checkout, the cart page, and the “My Account” page, for both guests and logged in customers.

You can also place it anywhere else on your site with the [tefw_exemption_form] shortcode.

Managing Exempt Customers & Orders

  • Exempt Customers – a searchable list of every customer claiming tax exemption, along with their details. Customers can be added and edited here directly.
  • Exempt Orders – every order placed with tax exemption, filterable by date.
  • If an order is marked as tax / VAT exempt, this will be shown on the admin order details page, where you can see the tax exempt details. An optional column on the orders list marks which orders were exempt.
  • Each customer’s exemption details can also be viewed and edited from their WordPress user profile.
  • Tax exemption details are included in WordPress personal data exports and erasure requests.

PRO Version

The PRO version offers several additional features including:

  • Registration number verification (VAT, charity, ABN, GSTIN and more).
  • Live lookups against the official registers – VIES, HMRC, the Australian Business Register and the Charity Commission.
  • Automatic approval for customers whose number verifies.
  • Consultation references recorded as proof that a number was checked.
  • Re-check a customer’s stored number at any time.
  • Option to show ex-tax prices to exempt customers across the whole store.
  • Optional “inc/ex tax” price toggle for every visitor.
  • Custom tax exemption form fields.
  • Tax exemption certificate upload field.
  • Tax exemption expiration date field.
  • Automatic expiry reminder & expired notification emails.
  • Customisable exemption request, approval and decline emails.
  • Default validity period (auto-calculate expiration dates).
  • Tax exemption city/state field.
  • Tax exemption fields on registration form.
  • Exemption status management for admins.
  • Only allow exemption for approved users.
  • Hide the tax exemption fields on checkout.
  • Only remove tax from specific products.
  • Only allow exemption for logged in users.
  • Only allow exemption for selected user roles.
  • Only allow exemption for selected countries.
  • Only allow exemption for selected states/cities.
  • Customize the tax class for each user.
  • Export CSV files of exempt customers.
  • Export CSV files of exempt orders.
  • Integration with “AvaTax”.
